title: Add type-ahead / autocomplete search
description:
Implement type-ahead search that shows suggestions as user types.

Requirements:
- Show dropdown of matching entries as user types (debounced, ~150ms)
- Highlight matching portion of text
- Keyboard navigation (up/down arrows, enter to select)
- Limit suggestions to top 10-15 matches
- Close on blur/escape

Implementation considerations:
- Debounce input to avoid excessive searches
- Use existing index search which already does substring matching
- Consider showing match count next to each suggestion
- Possibly use Lit's @lit-labs/task for async state management

UX flow:
1. User starts typing "del"
2. After 150ms pause, dropdown shows: "Dell (5,432)", "Delock (234)", ...
3. User can click or arrow-down + enter to select
4. Selection populates search box and triggers full search
close_reason: Implemented type-ahead autocomplete with debounced search, keyboard navigation, match highlighting, and count display

title: Implement multi-word index matching
description: Model matching should match each word against the index independently. If user types "DELL XXXXX", it should match entries where the model contains either "DELL" or "XXXXX". Users should be guided to enter only one word per dimension for best results.

title: Fixed search box with scrollable results pane
description:
The search box/tabs should remain fixed at the top while results scroll independently below.

Current: Entire page scrolls, search box scrolls out of view
Desired: Search box stays pinned, results pane scrolls internally

Implementation:
- Container with fixed height (e.g., calc(100vh - header))
- Search section: fixed/sticky at top
- Results section: overflow-y: auto, flex: 1

This enables future infinite scroll within the results pane without losing access to search controls.
close_reason: Implemented compact UI with fixed search section and scrollable results pane

title: Lazy-load indexes in web interface
description:
When searching via the web interface, only load indexes as required to minimize initial page load time.

Options:
1. Load on-demand: When user clicks a search tab (vendors, products, codes, sizes), show loading spinner while fetching that index
2. Progressive background loading: Load indexes in priority order after initial page load (e.g., products first since most common, then vendors, then sizes, then codes)

Index sizes for reference:
- vendors.idx: 254 KB
- products.idx: 802 KB  
- codes.idx: 1.2 MB
- sizes.idx: 228 KB

Implementation considerations:
- Use fetch() with appropriate caching headers
- Consider IndexedDB for client-side caching of loaded indexes
- Show loading state in UI when index not yet available
- Possibly prefetch on hover over tab
notes:
Progress bar UX implemented in commit 69205b0:
- Tabs show progress bar that fills during download
- Turns green at 100% when loaded
- Shows "Loading index..." in results area during download
- Search waits for index if not loaded, with proper UI feedback
close_reason: Implemented progressive background loading of indexes with visual progress indicators in each tab

title: Verify and ensure case-insensitive searching
description:
All index searches should be case-insensitive.

Current state: index-loader.js does `entry.keyLower.includes(queryLower)` which should handle this.

Verify:
- Searching "dell" matches "Dell" and "DELL"
- Searching "SAMSUNG" matches "Samsung"
- Works across all index types (products, vendors, codes, sizes)

Enhance if needed:
- Ensure consistent behavior across all search paths
- Add tests to verify case insensitivity

title: Responsive mobile view
description:
Add responsive CSS for mobile devices:
- Stack tabs vertically or use horizontal scroll
- Full-width search box
- Results and detail panel stack vertically
- Touch-friendly tap targets
- Consider bottom sheet for detail view on mobile

title: Switch from DuckDB to DuckLake for intermediate storage
description: Replace DuckDB with DuckLake (MotherDuck's open table format) for the intermediate storage format. DuckLake uses Parquet files which should be faster to build and easier to publish/distribute.
